judgments.justification: It reports “2.1 macro-F1 points,” the correct averages, paired test, p-value, confidence interval, and five-seed scope.
Only the cross-platform mean is reported; performance on Gildcrest, Nettlebank, and Pikestaff individually is not stated.
It states “higher…on all four subtypes” and reports the identity-attack values corresponding to the 3.7-point advantage.
Calling Cobble-Board “unseen” ignores its use for early stopping, checkpoint selection, and threshold choice, and its lack of a test partition.
“On the unseen Cobble-Board platform” mischaracterizes the tuned development set and fails to state that genuinely held-out platform generalization remains unanswered.
It reports the in-distribution average advantage—“81.9…vs 79.8”—and its significant paired seed-level comparison.
“On the unseen Cobble-Board platform” wrongly presents the tuning/development collection as unseen instead of stating that untuned platform transfer was not evaluated.
